events.text: Above the clouds the far shore is closer than it ever was below: a step out of the body on the high isle and you are standing on grey water with grey cloud over it, and the dead walking the bank are immortals, most of them.

effects.log: You walk down. The water does not wet you.

choices.text: Look back at your body on the isle

effects.log: It sits on the isle with its eyes closed, very small from here.
A few of them turn. One of them knows your name.

events.text: The Isles' archivists say the far shore lies just under the sea of clouds, and they are right: you sink through the clouds in your sleep and come out on a quiet bank where nothing hurts, not even the old crack in your core.

effects.log: You walk a long way. The bank goes on.
You sit. After a while the river begins to talk.
You go back up through the clouds. You will come again.

events.text: On the far shore below the clouds something is waiting that was an immortal once, ten thousand years ago. It has cultivated in the grey all that time, and it has been waiting for a soul to come down to it.

choices.text: Face it, and lay it to rest

effects.log: You face it until it remembers what it was, and lets go.
You take it into yourself. It is strong, and it is not kind.

choices.text: Burn cloud-incense and send it elsewhere

effects.log: The incense burns, and it goes elsewhere.
You flee up through the clouds into your body, and lie there shaking.

You stand beside {him} at the rail, and say nothing, and are glad.

events.text: There is no thunder above the clouds for this. Instead every kindness you ever did comes back up the cloud road as a test: the ones you saved, asking to be saved again, all in one season.

effects.log: You meet it, every test of it, and come out the other side.

choices.text: Bow under it: give much away

effects.log: You give and give until the debt is light enough to carry.

variants: The clouds under your isle go still for a season, and up the cloud road, one by one, come the ones your kindness once held up. Each asks again, a little more than before. Heaven is weighing what you are.
No storm gathers. Instead, every debt of kindness you were ever paid comes due at once, and the cloud road is never empty: the saved, the forgiven, the fed, all asking for the same hand again.
Heaven sends no lightning for this one. It sends your own good deeds back, all together, each one larger than you left it, and waits on the cloud road to see how much of you is still willing.

All season the skiffs keep mooring at your rail, and every passenger is someone you once helped, back again with a heavier need. There is no thunder. This is the whole of the trial: whether the hand is still open.

events.text: Your good karma has grown heavier than you are, and the Isles feel it: cranes land on your rail all season, each with a slip asking for help you once said you would always give.

effects.log: You meet it, every test of it, and come out the other side.

choices.text: Bow under it: give much away

effects.log: You give and give until the debt is light enough to carry.

variants: Your good karma has grown heavier than your golden core, and the Isles lean towards it. Petitions come on every skiff, in every crane's beak, and each one is a promise you once made.

For forty days the sky over your isle is a clean, hard blue. The old immortals say that is how it begins with the good ones: Heaven tests a full cup by shaking it, and every crane that lands on your rail brings a shake.
A whole isle of petitioners drifts up beside yours and moors there, and every one of them carries a slip in your own hand, a promise from some old year. Heaven is quiet. Heaven is watching.
Your merit sits on the Isles like a weight, and the Isles answer it. Every skiff that ties up at your quay brings someone who once heard you promise help, and now has come to collect.

events.text: The spring on your isle has gone cold and black, and there are handprints on the inside of your grotto's jade window in the morning, small ones and large ones. Your bad karma has come up through the clouds to visit.

effects.log: You go out to them, soul to soul.

events.text: A ferryman of the far shore hands you his pole without a word, the same pole his teacher handed him when the Isles were young, and steps off onto the bank to rest.

events.text: The marsh under the far shore's cliffs smells of iron and old lightning. The souls that sink in it fell from the Isles with their energy still in them, and it is all there for the taking.

events.text: You sit down on the shore below the clouds and stop doing anything at all. After a long time you notice the river has run around you, the way the clouds run around an isle.

effects.log: You begin, which is to say you go on sitting.

events.text: Lanterns coming down the river against the current, a long line of them: the wardens of the far shore have learned what an immortal has been eating in their marsh.
